description_text: The OBERLÄNDER is a basic type of the Middle Rhine ship, which of 15th up to 18th century was used mainly on the distance between Mainz and Cologne. Its shape is adapted to the particular circumstances of the current path and its fairway. The floor plan has the shape of a trapezoid. The greatest width is in the ship's bottom, and in the rear , the width of the 1.5 to 2 times the width of the bow. The floor is completely flat and is pulled up in the stern to a huge hut, which is pointed at a height of 6-7 m and steep drops to the deck. The deck has from bow to stern the same width and is completely flat. It falls against the bow. It gives the impression of heaviness, but this is not true. Top and bottom form an angle of up to 10 degrees. The 6-7 m high mast pole is used exclusively for towing. The viability of the Oberlander likely 100 - 120 t have not been exceeded. The round window is flush with the top strake, so that no transition board is available. The form shall bear halfway up two gangways, which served as the site of the Boating Party. The sites of Oberlander  were mainly in Bonn Beuel , to a lesser extent in Mainz on the Vilzbacher shipyard. Often the ships were used one or two times, than demolished to gain the wood for house construction.

The High Mobility Multipurpose Wheeled Vehicle (HMMWVl: Humvee) is a family of light, four-wheel drive, military trucksand utility vehicles produced by AM General.It has largely supplanted the roles previously performed by the original jeep, and others such as the Vietnam War-era M151 jeep, the M561 Gama Goat, their M718A1 and M792 ambulance versions, the Commercial Utility Cargo Vehicle (CUCV), and other light trucks. Primarily used by the United States military, it is also used by numerous other countries and organizations and even in civilian adaptations. The Humvee saw widespread use in the Gulf War of 1991, where it negotiated the treacherous desert terrain; this usage helped to inspire civilian Hummer versions.

description_text:
Our national and international success is based on our 25 years Know How in designing and producing high quality 2 – stroke engines. The 39 years of industrial experience of our designer had been realized in our new range of engines representing the latest state of the art of 2-stroke technology. Having this in mind a new generation of mufflers had to be developed suitable to handle the higher degree of saturation and process of combustion efficiency. 3W developed these new types of mufflers. Now 3W- Modellmotoren GmbH  is capable to deliver complete solutions of propulsion Systems.
3W-Engineering System
Use our Kow How and ask us for a quotation for your customs build engine.  Design is done by 3D-modeling using CAD Pro Engineer, prototype engines by using Lost Wax moulding and / or Rapid Prototyping , test runs and mass production in our facilities.
3W – History
1985    Introduction of the first 2-stroke gasoline engine especially designed for airplane models :  3W-60
1986    Development and production of 3W-40 and 3W-80B2 opposed twin
1987    Development and production of 3W-35 as well as the first 2-cylinder in-line-engine : 3W-80R2
1988    Development and production of : 3W-120B2
1989    Development and production of 3W-70B2 as well as the first 4-cylinder 3W-240B4 and  3W-160B4
1991 Development and production of : 3W-48B2
1992 Development and production of 2-cylinder in-line engine 3W-120R2 as well as 3-cylinder in-line engine 3W-120R3. Quique Somenzini demonstrates the first torque-roll using 3W-70B2 at the TOC  in Las Vegas.
1993 Development and production of 4-cylinder opposed 3W-140B4 and 3W-156B4
1994 Steve Stricker is the first pilot at the TOC , using a 4-cylinder opposed in his Extra with 3400 mm wing span : 3W-160B4.  Quique Somenzini won this TOC with 3W-120B2
1994 / 1996  Most popular and spectacular manoeuvre at the TOC : Torque Roll. Most used engine 3W-120B2
1995  Start of the new i-serie  representing a new cylinder and piston technology. First engines : 3W-70i   and  3W-75i
1996 Steve Stricker wins the TOC with 3W-160B4 build in his Extra with a wing span of 3400mm. Development and production of : 3W-50i , 3W78iB2 and 3W-100iB2.
1997  3W received the patent no. 4408908 for its 2-stroke 3-cylinder radial engine 3W-105STR31998 Our cooperation of many years with Quique Somenzinileads to the development of the: QS-Engine serie. Quique Somenzini wins the TOC with his new 3W-150iB2 QS engine with 4 real transfer ports. Start with the development and production of : 3W-240iB2 opposed twin.
1998   Start of 3W´s own airplane model serie. These models are developed in cooperation with the world best pilots and are produced exclusively for 3W. The design of these airplane models are influenced by Peter Weinhold´s long time experience and knowledge of having build over 500 various models. The finishing touch is given by doing intensive  flight test done by International Top Pilots like Wolfgang and Roland Matt. Both gentlemen are looking back at a long time experience in design and flying on top level.
1999 Quique Somenzini does the hat trick and wins again the TOC with 3W-150iB2 QS. Development of a flexible drive system for para glider  : 3W-240iB2 Para.
2000 Development of a custom made 4-cylinder flat with 33.32cu.in. / 546ccm.
2001 Development and production of : 3W-200iB2
2002 Patent application in Europe and USA for a new muffler system. Development and production of a new 4-cylinder flat : 3W-212iB4. The 3rd. generation of ignitions is released. The programmable on board micro processor allows a special auto timing  for our engines.
Technical specifications :   6,0V operation voltage, voltage range : 4,8V – 8,4 V
Temperature range : -40°C / + 65°C
Out put signal standard for connecting 3W´s digital RPM meter
2003    Design finished for the following engines : 3W-342iB2 , 2-cylinder flat; 3W-684iB4 , 4-cylinder flat, 3W-256 STR / 4-T , 5 cylinder radial, 4-stroke. Models : First prototypes of airplane models YAK 54 / 3050mm and Votec 322 / 3000mm are in the air for intensive test flying.
2004    At present 3W produces engines between : 1.46 and 41.74 cu.in. Twenty two different cylinder capacities are combined to forty seven different variations. Development and production of : 3W-28i / 3W-56iB2 and 3W-112iB4. Development of airplane model : PITTS S 12, wing span 3000mm.
2005    In the meantime 16 different airplane models are produced. Wing span range : 2000mm and 3950mm. To meet the special requirements of our international competition aerobatic pilots we deliver  certain models in a special light Competition Version. This means the fuselage is made in composite using Kevlar – Honeycombs . All rudders have holes to save weight. Reinforcements are done by using carbon material.
2006    3W arranged the 1st. Rookie meeting to promote youngsters. This opportunity was taken    to look for a new sponsor pilot for our team. Tim Stadler had been selected and since this year he is part of our team of sponsored pilots. Development and production  of : 3W-275xiB2
2007    Development and production of : 3W-210XIB2. Development of Heavy Fuel Engines ( HFE )
2008    Development and production of : 3W-110iR2. Production and testing of 4 different HF engines : 3W-28iHFE / 3W-56iB2 HFE / 3W-110IB2TS HFE / 3W-157xiB2TS HFE.
2009    Development and production of : 3W-55xi. Development and production of : 3W-210xiB2 TS HFE
3W is the only Model Engine Manufacturer producing 4-cylinder and 6-cylinder 2-stroke flat engines. Competitors  copied our engines and ignitions but with limited success. These plagiarisms are based on our technology of our 3W-80B2 and 3W-120B2 which were developed in 1986 and 1988.Our current engine technology is generations way off from this old technology. In a continues  process our R &D department optimises the running characteristics, power and reliability.
3W is proud in being able to offer excellent flying airplane models well engineered. Useful accessories, mainly designed by 3W and produced for 3W complete the program.
Ignition System
3W-ignition systems and electronic components are designed and produced according to Industry Standards. Modern RISC –processor technology as well as selected components and a comprehensive Quality Control are the heard of a reliable system. The modellers benefit from specifications which are usually done for the industry. The ignition systems are laid out for a wide temperature range of : -40°C / +65°C. Suitable timing curves with automatic timing are standard with all 3W-engines as well as a strict quality control of all electronic parts. Several developments are tested momentarily and will set a new standard for 3W-Modellmotoren GmbH respectively power, reliability and life time.
Read more http://www.3w-modellmotoren.com/service/about-us.html

description_text:
Hello Friends,
A short story... When I was 8 years old I had a home-made go-cart. I drove it so much I finally broke the connecting rod and the engine died.   =(    My father owned an automotive repair shop and he ordered a new connecting rod for my Briggs & Stratton engine without letting me know. I awoke one morning to find the new connecting rod in a box sitting on our kitchen counter. It was like Christmas Morning !!!!
After school I raced to his shop to begin the repair. He offered no assistance but I soon had the engine running like new. He was impressed. Soon after, he brought me into his shop and showed me a 4 cylinder Jeep engine hanging on an engine stand. It was an old flat-head 4 WWII military engine.
He said "I want you to rebuild this engine".  I balked and said "I can't do that!".  He said this engine is just the same as the one you just worked on, but four cylinders instead of just one. Okay....    I'll Try.   He watched over my shoulder and instructed me on how to use his valve grinding machine. Honing the cylinders, using new bearings, Facing the heads to flatten them, etc...
I was 8 years old and I had just completely rebuilt a four cylinder flat head engine by myself.  I will never forget that week.
This story is about my life, and my Father passing down his vast knowledge of combustion engines to me.  A true gift.  He is now 87 years old and I am 58. I still ask him to explain any information about drive trains, transmissions, steering alignments, etc.  My Father is a TRUE Master Mechanic!

description_text:
i'll add the upcomming things we'll do on this projecthere i will list the folders in the project in chronological order and tell how much time we had to do it, and what exactly we had to do
1 tiny race car on catia (2 month) : from several physical limitations (space for engine, battery, overall max size, ect...) we had to do a wooden car from a side view and top view drawing we also had to do. there is 2 vers because the first was while learning catia, and the 2nd what we had to give (the full model are the "MY_e-RACECAR_PROJECT" files)
2 valve (3h) : had to reproduce on solidworks the "wheel" and the cap from a technical drawing
3 robot hand (6h) : we had all the pieces except what hold the fingers and "base", so we had to do this piece from the dimmensions of the other, then assemble all of it and do an animation of it operating
4 fixed support of 'pieces holder' (idk how it is called in english) (3h) : we had to do the top piece of this http://goo.gl/uigcPLbut without having pics of it, just knowing that the 2 "holding plates" should match and make the metal bar fit, and have it as light as possible but still strong enough in plastic. and then do a static simulation
5 duct tape dispenser (9h) : we had to do something that can hold the tape ring when it is full and empty + that can cut it in some ways + to have a design in "characters" "animals" or "transportation" themes.first with modeling clay then on solidworks, and if the dispenser is good enough it might get 3D printedhere is the technical drawing : http://goo.gl/bqTX9G

title: Transformable bicycle seat Free 3D model

description_text:
This is a product designed for the »velodroom«  competition.
THE BASIC IDEA: The bar that is connecting the bicycle seat and the bicycle frame would be transformable to a 3 legged stool.
THE CONCEPT: The bar would be made out 3 parts, each presenting a third of the connected bar. Two parts of the bar would be connected to a scissors like structure and the third part would be able to rotate between them. The seat would have 4 holes, one for the  connected bar which would be used while cycling and 3 for the three different parts,used  when sitting.
USAGE OF THE IDEA: I had this unique idea in my head for a long time and this  competition gave me the opportunity to show it in my prototype.  How I came up with this? Even if you lock your bicycle, in big cities people will still steal your seats. Thats why many people remove their seats to avoid this problem. Also in big cities some distances are just to big to be traveled by bicycle, thats why you have to combine your riding with traveling by bus or train. From my own experience I can tell, that many times you have to wait from 30 to 60 minutes for your train or bus to come. It is much easier to spend this time sitting then standing. So I combines this 2 problems and came up with this solution. This product would be also very useful when traveling in nature. Sometimes you want to sit down, but you can not do that on wet grounds or muddy terrain. So this would be very intereseting for mountain bikers.
As far as I know, my prototype is unique, I have never seen anything like it or heard of any idea even close to mine. I know that my idea is very strange, but I am sure that people would be interested in it, because most of them rather sit then stand.

title: Dynamo Recharger for velodroom  Free 3D model
formats_detail: [{"format": "PDF", "full_name": "PDF", "file_size": "8.27 MB", "file_count": 2, "version": null, "renderer": null}, {"format": "IGE", "full_name": "IGES", "file_size": "2.73 MB", "file_count": 1, "version": null, "renderer": null}, {"format": "SLDPRT", "full_name": "SolidWorks", "file_size": "7.59 MB", "file_count": 1, "version": null, "renderer": null}, {"format": "OTHER", "full_name": "Other", "file_size": "704 KB", "file_count": 1, "version": null, "renderer": null}]
total_file_size: PDF:8.27 MB, IGE:2.73 MB, SLDPRT:7.59 MB, OTHER:704 KB
description_text:
This is my idea for the  “velodroom” competition.
A FEW DETAILS:The basic idea: To recharge your electronic devices while cycling. The system should be as simple as possible, fastly removable and easy to store in your pocket or bag.
The concept:The whole idea consists of 3 basic parts: The GSM/GPS holder,  the dynamo and the cable with 1-2 exta straps (which are not included in the SolidWorks files).
The Physical principle:  The electricity produced while cycling would not be constant, so it would be necessary to incorporate an electric regulator which would limit the voltage. The rechargable system would work via USB.
Why is this idea any different from already used solutions?Exactly, this principle has already been used by NOKIA, but my idea has a few special features that connect your design and usage. The Nokia system is based on a fixed position of the dynamo, mine is not and is easly removable.
The drawings: I did my basic design by hand, also the picture is taken with not the best camera, but the concept is clear.
My idea has 4 special features:1.  The dynamo would not be at a fixed position, it would be connected to the bar the same way as your light, this way you could easly regulate its position.2.  The connection between the dynamo and the holder (that is connected to the bar) would be a bit different. They would be connected with a spring that would push them together (drawing 2 and 3), the touching surface would not be flat, but there would be integrated a circular sprocket on both surfaces (holder and dynamo).  This way you could rotate the dynamo head to the best position possible with a »click click« motion.3.  The dynamo head would be a little spherical (drawing 2), so it would be easier to adjust the head position and this way to insure a good grip.4.  The cable would not be at a fixed lenght, but it would be adjustable by the same system as used in measuring tapes. You could pull out to the lenght needed and when you would remove the system, you could contract the cable by pushing the red botton (drawing 2),
I did not put much effort in the design of the electric device holder. There is shown just an idea, where you could connect a phone or GPS with the holder by using 2 rubber straps, but I am sure there  are many better ways that would allow to lockout devices in all different shapes and sizes. I would also attach 2 velcro straps on the cable. This way you could link the cable with the bicycle bars. The velcro straps should be able to move up and down the cable.
NOTE: The cable is not very admirable, it just shows how it should be connected :) This goes for the whole system, this is just my perspective and idea, there are many ways to use the same principle in a more effective way, I am sure about that!

title: Bauer Drop-Down Trailer Free 3D model
formats_detail: [{"format": "SLDPRT", "full_name": "SolidWorks", "file_size": "61.9 MB", "file_count": 1, "version": null, "renderer": null}]
total_file_size: SLDPRT:61.9 MB
description_text:
BACKGROUND:The idea behind this proposal is to produce a compact, light-weight design, with a particular focus on a drive-on lead-in angle that can support any height of car. A 3° angle has been achieved when mounted to a towing vehicle, and the possibility to lie entirely flat when in storage.
LIFTING/LOWERING:A centrally placed hydraulic pump feeds the pistons (one attached to each Lifting Unit) that extend to lower the platform, and compress to lift. A reservoir is attached to the pump to provide the necessary fluids. The shown design uses an electrical system to run the hydraulics, however, it would be no trouble to replace this with a manual pump if simplicity is required.
SUSPENSION:To ensure the trailer takes as little space as possible, I wanted to keep the overall width of the product really slim. For this reason, the suspension is mounted above the wheels allowing them to press right up against the platform. A mountain bike like system is used, with a central suspension pivot arm to transfer the vertical wheel movement. Although it looks as if the wheels will catch on the fenders, there is plenty of space under there for bouncing around :)
WIDTH: 2816mmLENGTH: 5330mmLEAD-IN ANGLE: 3 degreesRIDE HEIGHT: 225mm
SOLIDWORKS ASSEMBLY:The native SW files are fully adjustable. Not in the main assembly, however. You must open individual assembly files to control different aspects of the design.Track Height: Open the "HYDRAULIC-PISTON" Assembly, and slide the "PISTON UPPER MOUNT" to change the height of the main car tracks. The piston tubing files will automatically update with the change of the piston extension.Suspension: Open the "SUSPENSION ASSEMBLY" file, then "SUSPENSION-COIL". By changing the height of the spiral curve in this part file, the suspension itself will compress or extend in the overall assembly file.Jockey Wheel: Simply open the "JOCKEY WHEEL ASSEMBLY" file, and play around with the height and rotation of the wheel.
UPDATES:The STEP files can be viewed in both raised and lowered versions for those without SolidWorks (please see TRAILER-ASSEMBLED_lowered.rar, and TRAILER-ASSEMBLED_lifted.rar).

description_text:
A shell for a pinewood derby car in the shape of a roadster, more or less following the look of the 1949 Snowberger-Offy Indianapolis 500 racecar.  The shell will drop on top of a standard pinewood derby wood block, which only needs a small bit of sawing (see the instructions).   
March 29, 2014:  Updated version 7 cleans up the exhaust area and adds four holes in the underside to accomodate standard pinewood derby cylindrical weights.   
April 12, 2014:  Updated STL of the body is "roadster_body.stl" and includes support structures underneath.  Use this version if you don't trust your slicer to generate proper support structures (I don't).  The photographs are from this version.  If you notice two notches along the side, they are for an exhaust pipe (STL forthcoming, probably in a few days).  
April 21, 2014:  See also my derivative Thing #305925.  Designed as a model/toy instead of a pinewood derby shell, it still has the same wheelbase and the body can be used interchangeably with the pinewood base described here.  There are also some useful accessories like exhaust pipes.  
Print with plenty of support.  See the photos for an example of removable support structures under the print.

title: LifeTrac Quick Connect Module Free 3D model
formats_detail: [{"format": "STP", "full_name": "STEP", "file_size": "5.71 MB", "file_count": 1, "version": null, "renderer": null}]
total_file_size: STP:5.71 MB
description_text:
Here is my idea for the LifeTrac Quick connect Module. My approach is very simple and low cost, but I think it could work. It has a modular geometry that can be assembled in a short time.
I’m maintaining the original model with the two bearing housing and the Hydraulic motor at the third connection point, even if it’s a difficult or a somewhat inconvenient configuration.
The reason for this is that I think that it’s important to maintain the most stable and rigid support possible for the axle system. For the current structure/chassis, it’s critical to use both horizontal square tubes as base for the transmission components.  Additionally, the spacing between the supports is short and the alignment can be adjusted at assembly.
As requested, I made my design modular and easily interchangeable with other equipment. In order to make it easy and quick to disassemble, I incorporated two special nuts that tighten two bolts at the same time. These nuts have a right hand thread on one side and a left hand thread at the other, and when it’s rotated, it tightens or loosens the two bolts simultaneously. (This arrangement can be overridden and regular bolts and nuts can be used to attach the system to the chassis).
My model allows reusing the current holes in the horizontal Tubes, the ones that were used for the original mounting plates. The only additional holes will be for the two “pin guides” at the bottom plate of the module.
Regarding the failure of the motor coupling; as I see it, occurred because the huge torque was transmitted by a single Keyway, (At least the most important reason). I did some calculations and determined that a parallel spline connection for the 1-1/4” diameter shaft of the motor shown in the link, and a 6 spline 1-3/4” diameter spline connection for the axle, could transmit the torque given by the mentioned motor. Both splines have a 2-1/4” length. The coupling material has to be Alloyed Steel. However, I think more information has to be considered in order to calculate this with more precision.
Any comment/feedback is most welcome
/MECA

description_text:
Here is my design. It's the same concept as many others, just different geometry for parts.
The parts are designed focusing on material reduction and simple geometry, in order to require easy bend procedures and produce more parts per sheet of metal. Check the Parts List file to observe required parts (Look under “Description” column, the ones that say: “Manufacturing Required”). The list also specifies all standard parts such as U-bolts, Hex bolts, Nuts and Washers.
I did some FE stress analysis to check the axle’s load capacity. The square Tube (50x50x3) resists the 1850 kg load and a maximum braking torque per wheel of 575 N.m, with a safety factor of 2. The Spring Support was also analyzed. The material used was ASTM A36, Yield Strength 250MPa.
The only welded part is the Torsion Support, which is welded to the axle square tube.
A couple of design revisions can be performed to tune up the model if needed.
Any comments/feedback are welcome.
Cheers!

The sale of nylon tires was started in 1959, and work forged ahead with the construction of the new Tokyo plant, which was opened in 1960, in order to cope with the fast-expanding market for motorization.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 8 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 It belongs to 3 companies, it is one of the most futuristic ever concepts, it is the best of it's kind.... it is.............K-Loft®..! K-L features touch-screen monitoring systems, control system similar to a flight simulator, and it is made out of aluminium! If you play a flight sim, this will be VERY easy to control! It has control systems as easy as possible and automated. Autopilot searches the destination in the world, and then it says if it exists or not. Then, you press the Turn on A/P button and it automatically travels you there. Although, you can control the speed and correct the path a little. It makes a virtual path for manual traveling, and it tells you where to turn or go straight. Systems from World Dynamics, engines/control systems from Boeing, %26 materials from AeroCraft! It is not fuel powered and it is just working until you're there, making its range unlimited! The engines just start producing a special sphere, which then launches a large anti-gravity ray that pulls the aircraft away from ground. It is being tilted by the amount of anti-gravity inside the sphere. When the sphere reduces it, the part of the fuselage that the engine lifts starts to go down just a little. It has a white-pink interior for added coziness...lol!

The Opebus has soft anti-gravity system above it's belly that slightly lifts the Opebus to an altitude of 10 feet. Then it slowly starts to move towards the next stop. The Opebus will be used manily in Crowne Springs.

description_text: This 3D model was originally created with Sketchup 13 and then converted to all other 3D formats. Native format is .skp 3dsmax scene is 3ds Max 2016 version, rendered with Vray 3.00 Welcome to the famed Paulwall Teapot, the largest teapot in all of Paulwall. Well, and the most abandoned one too! What could be sadder? Who would abandon their teapot like that? Well, obviously someone who's invested business in Paulwall for a while. The teapot, built in 1922, is Paulwall's oldest standing gas station. Yes, used to house the fuel to get your cars on the road! Such historical significance but as like several other historically significant structures in Paulwall, they went vacant. But this is one of the last standing buildings left on its block. There used to be 2 motels (across street), both gone, a neon tin-clad silver diner (next door) which is also gone as well as the vanishing of other stores and houses. There used to be large industrial warehouse type structures behind this teapot that are now gone so because all those buildings are gone, from here to the train tracks, you'd get an uninterrupted view of the buildings of downtown Paulwall. Creepy area to be at night, never go alone and probably shouldn't get out of your car either. Holes in the pavement on each side of the gas pumps show where the canopy used to be. The station changed hands so you don't see the original retro pumps. Abandoned since the 90's. Enjoy and please rate :)
